prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D survivor animation for the existing Grave Accord game. Image 1 is the approved Tank identity reference in four views. Image 2 is the edit target: the new four-frame directional idle strip. Replace its four idle poses with the four firearm-attack poses described below while retaining this exact facing and identity. Draw one complete NORTH firearm attack animation strip, using the same character, same costume, same palette and same proportions. Output exactly FOUR full-body frames, in one horizontal row of four equally spaced cells on a wide genuinely transparent canvas, ideally about 2048 by 512. Every figure faces NORTH, away from the viewer, matching the lower-left back figure of image 1 and the matching idle poses in image 2. Show the back of the head and the red hood resting behind the neck, crossed back straps and long coat panels. Do not show a face or add a mask to the back of the head. Fill the four cells; no second row. Preserve the short brown hair, same dark iron face mask, rust-red long coat and hood resting behind the neck, crossed brown straps, iron shoulder/forearm/knee guards, dark trousers and heavy boots. The tall shield remains in the physical LEFT hand, which is viewer LEFT in this back view; show its plain wooden/leather back and straps exactly as the back reference, without adding a front cross to its back. The firearm remains in the physical RIGHT hand, viewer RIGHT. Do not swap, duplicate, melt or bend the equipment. Keep broad matte red cloth planes, three major value masses, crisp selective hand-drawn black ink contours and restrained opaque gouache shading. Match the existing reference finish without adding dense scratches, texture noise, decorative filigree, glossy gradients, glow, smoke or particles. Action sequence: frame 1 planted ready guard with the firearm low, matching the established upright silhouette; frame 2 smoothly raises the SAME firearm in its SAME physical right hand to aim in the character's facing direction while keeping the shield close on the left arm; frame 3 one restrained recoil through wrist and shoulder, still gripping the same rigid firearm with no duplicate barrel; frame 4 lowers and recovers toward the exact frame-1 guard. Both boots stay planted on one baseline. Keep the first frame's head-to-sole size and all limb proportions constant throughout; the aiming/recoil change should be visible but controlled. Keep the shield structurally identical in all frames. Hands remain connected to their forearms; no weapon floats through the shield. Keep body height and camera angle constant across all four frames, give each silhouette clear transparent gutters and generous padding, and align both boots to one common ground baseline. No running, turning, muzzle flash, sparks, smoke, attack particles or dramatic cape movement. The game adds the projectile separately. No floor, scenery, shadow oval, checker pattern, labels, numbers, grid lines or text. Preserve actual alpha transparency. Deliver one coherent hand-drawn four-frame attack strip, not separate illustrations.

CORRECTION FOR THIS WHOLE NORTH STRIP: This is a BACK VIEW aiming NORTH, toward the TOP edge of the image. Image 3 is the rejected attack attempt: its middle poses point the gun horizontally to screen right, which is the wrong direction. Regenerate the complete four-frame strip with the same Tank identity and planted boots. In frames 2 and 3, the physical right elbow lifts forward/away and the gun aims UPWARD and AWAY into the top of the scene, foreshortened just outside the right shoulder. The weapon's projected long axis should be nearly vertical/up-screen; do not extend the right arm sideways. Its muzzle opening is not facing the viewer. Retain the red hood/back of the head, left-arm shield at viewer left with its plain strapped back, and the four-frame ready/aim/recoil/recover sequence. All four figures remain north facing, never show the front face or the shield cross, never point right or left. Keep generous gutters.
